title: Formal etaleness of algebraic spaces is local on compatible etale scheme charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For any morphism $g:A\to B$ of algebraic spaces over $S$ (including schemes), write $P(g)$ for the following property: for every first order thickening $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] and every pair $a_0:T_0\to A$, $b:T\to B$ of $S$-morphisms with $g a_0=bj$, there exists exactly one $a:T\to A$ with $aj=a_0$ and $ga=b$. Then $P(f)$ holds if and only if $P(h)$ holds for every commutative diagram $v h=f u$, where $U,V$ are $S$-schemes, $u:U\to X$ and $v:V\to Y$ are representable etale morphisms, and $h:U\to V$ is an $S$-morphism. Here representable etale means that every base change to a scheme is a scheme with etale projection [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. No etaleness, finite presentation, separation, or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed on $f$.

source.place: Tag 04GD (lemma-formally-etale), equivalence (1) and (2); formal etaleness is expanded as the affine square-zero lifting property of definition-formally-smooth-etale-unramified.

proof.text: First consider any representable etale map $q:A\to B$ of algebraic spaces. Given a first order thickening $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of schemes and a lifting square for $q$, the scheme $E=T\times_B A$ is etale over $T$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The initial lift is a section $s_0:T_0\to E_0=E\times_TT_0$. By [lem-sfb-space-thickening-etale-scheme-equivalence], restriction on morphisms between the two etale $T$-schemes $T$ and $E$ is bijective. Thus $s_0$ extends to exactly one $T$-map $T\to E$, which is a section because its codomain is an object over $T$. Projection to $A$ gives the desired unique lift. This proves $P(q)$, and indeed the same assertion for arbitrary scheme tests. Here first order thickenings are thickenings by [def-sbc-first-order-thickening].

Suppose $P(f)$ and fix $vh=fu$ as in the statement. For a square $ha_0=bj$ with affine test $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, first lift $ua_0$ uniquely along $f$ over $vb$, obtaining $x:T\to X$. Step 1 lifts $a_0$ uniquely along $u$ over $x$, obtaining $a:T\to U$. The maps $ha,b:T\to V$ have the same restriction $ha_0$ and the same image under $v$; step 1 applied to $v$ therefore gives $ha=b$. Any other lift has the same image $x$ by $P(f)$ and then equals $a$ by step 1 for $u$. Thus $P(h)$ for every diagram. This is the explicit composition and cancellation argument: it does not assert that the given chart square is cartesian.

source.place: Tag 04GD, lemma-formally-etale, (1) implies (2); composition and Tag 04G5, lemma-formally-permanence (2)

proof.text: Conversely suppose $P(h)$ for every compatible diagram. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $v:V\to Y$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The last assertion of [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] supplies a scheme $U$, a representable surjective etale atlas $u:U\to X$, and $h:U\to V$ with $vh=fu$. The hypothesis gives $P(h)$. The composite $k=fu=vh$ has $P(k)$: in any affine test square for $k$, first use step 1 for $v$ to lift the initial $V$-map over the prescribed $Y$-map, then $P(h)$ to lift to $U$. Uniqueness follows in the same order, first after applying $h$, then in $U$. Neither $h$ nor $f$ is assumed etale.

source.place: Tag 04GD, lemma-formally-etale, choice of diagram (3) and composition in (3) implies (1)

proof.text: Fix an affine lifting test $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, $a_0:T_0\to X$, $b:T\to Y$ for $f$. The pullback $W_0=T_0\times_{a_0,X,u}U$ is a scheme surjective etale over $T_0$, with tautological map $c_0:W_0\to U$, by the scheme-test meaning of $u$ in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-thickening-etale-scheme-equivalence] to $j$ to obtain an etale scheme $W\to T$ and an isomorphism $W\times_TT_0\cong W_0$. The map $W\to T$ is surjective: the composite $W_0\to W\to T$ is already surjective since $W_0\to T_0$ and $T_0\to T$ are. Choose affine opens $W_\lambda$ covering $W$. Their reductions $W_{0\lambda}=W_\lambda\times_TT_0$ are affine first order thickenings inside $W_\lambda$: locally their rings are $C/IC$, with $(IC)^2=0$, where $I^2=0$ defines $j$. Thus these are legitimate affine tests for $P(k)$. The family $W_\lambda\to T$ is a jointly surjective etale family (open immersions are etale, and etale maps compose), hence an fppf covering by the definitions of etale and fppf covering.

source.place: Tag 04CY, lemma-etale-on-top, construction of W and W prime; Tag 05ZS; affine refinement and square-zero base change

proof.text: First prove uniqueness of a lift along $f$ for the fixed test. If $x,y:T\to X$ are two lifts, step 1 for $u$ on $W_{0\lambda}\hookrightarrow W_\lambda$ extends $c_0|_{W_{0\lambda}}$ to maps $c_x,c_y:W_\lambda\to U$ over $x|_{W_\lambda},y|_{W_\lambda}$, respectively. Both maps lie over $b|_{W_\lambda}$ for $k$ and have the same reduction. Since $P(k)$, they are equal; hence $x,y$ agree on every $W_\lambda$. They are equal on $T$ because $X$ is an fppf sheaf and this family is an fppf covering. Explicitly, the sheaf equalizer of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $X(T)\to\prod_\lambda X(W_\lambda)$ injective. This proves uniqueness for affine tests. It also proves uniqueness for a first order thickening $Z_0\hookrightarrow Z$ with arbitrary scheme $Z$: restrict to affine opens of $Z$ (the reductions are affine), apply the just-proved affine uniqueness, and use the same sheaf separatedness on that Zariski, hence fppf, cover.

source.place: Tag 04CY, lemma-etale-on-top (5), uniqueness, including affine refinement of nonaffine tests

proof.text: Now apply $P(k)$ to each $W_{0\lambda}\hookrightarrow W_\lambda$ and $c_0|_{W_{0\lambda}}$ over $b|_{W_\lambda}$. Obtain $c_\lambda:W_\lambda\to U$ and put $x_\lambda=uc_\lambda$. On each overlap $Z=W_\lambda\times_TW_\mu$, the two maps $x_\lambda|_Z,x_\mu|_Z$ lie over $b|_Z$ and reduce to $a_0|_{Z_0}$, where $Z_0=Z\times_TT_0$. Its ideal is again square zero by the local calculation in step 4. Step 5, which allows nonaffine $Z$, gives equality. The sheaf equalizer for $X$ therefore glues the $x_\lambda$ to $x:T\to X$. On the same fppf covering $fx=b$, so sheaf separatedness for $Y$ gives $fx=b$ globally. On its base change $W_{0\lambda}\to T_0$, the equality $xj=a_0$ holds, so separatedness for $X$ gives $xj=a_0$. The base-changed family is an fppf covering by the site axioms in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Step 5 gives uniqueness of $x$. Thus $P(f)$, completing the reverse implication. No affineness of overlaps or global section of an atlas was assumed.
